TRANSPARENT BY DESIGN

What makes a candidate?

A stock must be above its 50-session average, have a positive 20-session return, and beat SPY over the same 63-session window.

This is an unvalidated research rule. It does not evaluate valuation, earnings surprises, or trader skill.

GET CONNECTED

Set up your scout.

One daily scan. Your sources. A record you can check.

01

Create your GitHub repository

Create a repository named market-scout, then add the starter project. The full instructions are in its README.

GitHub Pages sites are normally public. Keep account balances, personal information, and private source content out of published data.

Open GitHub ↗
02

Connect market data

Create an Alpaca paper account and generate paper API keys. In GitHub, open Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions and add these two repository secrets:

ALPACA_API_KEYALPACA_SECRET_KEY

Never paste keys into this website, your repository files, or a chat. This project only reads market data.

Open Alpaca ↗
03

Run the scan and publish

In GitHub Settings → Pages, choose GitHub Actions as the source. Add the repository variable ENABLE_PAGES with the value true under Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables. Then open Actions → Scan and publish → Run workflow. Scheduled scans run Tuesday–Saturday at 02:17 UTC, after the preceding U.S. trading day.

A schedule can run late. Always check the scan time and each stock’s date before using the results.

04

Choose the sources worth following

Edit config/sources.json with RSS or Atom feed URLs you have permission to use. The starter leaves this empty until you choose your traders.

Version 1 detects explicit stock cashtags such as $AAPL. A mention is not treated as a recommendation. AI interpretation and trader performance scoring are later steps.
